result.summary: This PR adds a Windows-only functional test verifying that the bitcoin.exe wrapper correctly forwards a spawned bitcoind child's exit code, distinguishing a genuine child exit of -1 from an actual spawn failure. It is a stacked follow-up to #36105, which contains the actual runtime fix (switching from _spawnvp(_P_WAIT) to _P_NOWAIT + _cwait); this PR's net diff still includes those commits until it is rebased after #36105 merges. It also re-enables previously Windows-skipped tests (tool_bitcoin.py, interface_gui.py) and adds a launch-failure test case requested during review.
result.problem: The original Windows wrapper implementation conflated a failed spawn with a child that legitimately exited with code -1, both returning -1 from _spawnvp(_P_WAIT), causing the wrapper to report a bogus startup error instead of forwarding the real exit code. This PR's test catches that regression and would have failed against the earlier faulty implementation, and it also verifies the complementary case (a real launch failure is still reported correctly).

result.card: This is a Windows-only functional test PR, stacked on and dependent on #36105, verifying that the bitcoin.exe wrapper correctly forwards a spawned bitcoind child's exit code (including the tricky -1 case) rather than conflating it with a launch failure. It also re-enables two previously Windows-skipped tests (tool_bitcoin.py, interface_gui.py) now that the underlying spawn logic waits for the child properly. The problem is a real regression class: the original _spawnvp(_P_WAIT) approach returned -1 for both a failed spawn and a legitimate child exit of -1, which the author demonstrates by showing the test fails against the pre-fix launcher and passes against the fixed one. Review state is Ready, with reviewer cyb3ralbert requesting and then verifying an additional launch-failure test case, followed by an ACK after testing on Linux and Windows across both CRTs; agreement is Strong with no objections. Because the actual runtime fix lives in #36105, this PR's own priority rests mainly on unblocking Windows CI coverage rather than fixing the bug itself.
